map.name: Manhunt
map.testedVersion: Selected-artifact Manhunt v1.0.0 source/package audit; SHA-256 c666000de5cd052288b00953baf9dc00410a65c6da53c16fb1e31b8e396025f3. Findings are promoted only from the selected Manhunt artifact plus current Manhunt Guide; historical reports are search pressure, not proof.

bugs.title: Arena 6 is materially incomplete compared with the canonical arena replica
bugs.problem: Arena 6 does not physically match the replicated arena structure used by Arenas 1–5 even though gameplay coordinates are generated from the same canonical arena template.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: Manhunt defines six fixed arenas that share the same translated gameplay layout. Arena 6 is expected to be a physical replica of that layout, but current-world sampling shows a material concentration of expected structure replaced by air in Arena 6 while Arenas 1–5 remain near parity.
bugs.impact: Players assigned to Arena 6 can receive a materially different or incomplete play space from other arenas. Paths, cover, chase routes, trap placement opportunities, and physical boundaries can therefore differ even though the game logic treats Arena 6 as equivalent.
reproduction: Start Manhunt in Arena 6 and compare its playable structure with the corresponding translated area in Arena 1.
Follow equivalent routes and structures using the same relative arena coordinates.
Inspect areas where the canonical replica contains solid structure.
Confirm that Arena 6 contains materially missing geometry/air where the equivalent canonical arena contains blocks.
bugs.expected: Arena 6 should physically reproduce the same canonical arena geometry and playable routes as Arenas 1–5 after coordinate translation.
bugs.observed: Current artifact parity evidence shows Arena 6 with approximately 5.62% / 6,207 sampled voxel mismatches, dominated by canonical structure becoming air; Arenas 1–5 are approximately 0–0.12%.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Gameplay configuration translates one canonical arena coordinate model across all six arenas, so the physical Arena 6 divergence is not represented as an intentional alternate layout in the selected source.

relevantCode.reason: All six arena gameplay coordinates are generated from the same canonical base positions through arena translation.

bugs.suggestedFix: Repair/rebuild Arena 6 from the canonical arena replica and revalidate geometry parity before treating it as an equivalent playable arena.

bugs.title: Some Hunters lose compass tracking when active Runners are fewer than Hunters
bugs.problem: Compass target assignment forbids reuse of a Runner target within the same refresh, so Hunters processed after all unique Runner targets are consumed receive no tracking state.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: Every active Hunter is given a tracking compass as a core role capability. The allocator enforces unique targets but has no fallback that permits multiple Hunters to track the last remaining Runner, causing valid Hunters to lose the role capability solely because the Runner count dropped below the Hunter count.
bugs.impact: Late in a multi-Hunter round, one Hunter may track the final Runner while the remaining Hunters receive no compass target. This weakens Hunter coordination precisely when few Runners remain and makes identical Hunter roles behave differently.
reproduction: Start a Manhunt round with a player count that produces multiple Hunters, such as 9 or 12 players with 3 Hunters.
Allow the round to progress until only one active Runner remains.
Wait for the next compass refresh interval.
Hold the tracking compass on each Hunter and compare target feedback.
Confirm that at most one Hunter retains the Runner target while later Hunters have no tracking state.
bugs.expected: Every active Hunter should retain a usable tracking target whenever at least one active Runner remains; target reuse should be allowed when unique Runner targets are exhausted.
bugs.observed: Target allocation uses a per-refresh used-target Set. If no unused Runner remains, trackingByHunterId for that Hunter is deleted and processing continues without a fallback target.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The unique-target allocator is the only current compass target allocator. No secondary reuse or shared-last-Runner path exists.

relevantCode.reason: Yu()/Zu() exclude already-used Runner IDs and delete a Hunter tracking entry when no unused candidate exists.

bugs.suggestedFix: Prefer unique Runner targets while enough Runners exist, then fall back to a valid active Runner for any remaining Hunters instead of deleting tracking state.

bugs.title: Transient disconnect removes a participant from the active round and can decide the winner immediately
bugs.problem: The gameplay disconnect path removes the player from round.players instead of preserving the participant as temporarily offline, then immediately re-evaluates terminal conditions.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: The surrounding party system defines a three-minute disconnected-member recovery window, but the active Manhunt round does not preserve the participant for that recovery. Both leave/disconnect aliases call the same destructive removal function, so a temporary connection loss is treated as permanent round departure.
bugs.impact: A last Runner disconnect can immediately award the round to Hunters; a last Hunter disconnect can award it to Runners. The removed participant can also disappear from round/session role and survival history, so a brief network interruption can alter winner, statistics, and later Hunter rotation.
reproduction: Start an active Manhunt round with at least one Hunter and Runner.
Disconnect the last active Runner while the round timer is still running; separately repeat with the last Hunter.
Observe the canonical round state and winner evaluation immediately after disconnect.
Reconnect within the configured three-minute party recovery window.
Confirm that the participant was already removed from the gameplay round and the terminal result can already have been committed.
bugs.expected: A recoverable transient disconnect should preserve the participant's round identity/state for the configured recovery window and should not decide the winner until the disconnect policy actually expires.
bugs.observed: ca and ya both alias da(); da() removes the player from round.players, clears role state, and the caller immediately runs be() win evaluation.
bugs.aiAnalysis: No normal disconnect path was found that sets player.online=false while retaining the player in the active round. The persisted model supports online state, but current disconnect mutation removes the participant instead.

relevantCode.reason: da() removes participants; ca=da and ya=da; Wa()/je() immediately evaluate the round after mutation.

bugs.suggestedFix: Separate temporary disconnect from intentional/permanent leave. Preserve round membership with online=false during the recovery window and apply terminal removal only when recovery expires or the player explicitly exits.

bugs.title: Placed Honey Trap gameplay state is not restored or reconciled when an active round is recovered after runtime reload
bugs.problem: Placed trap state and trap-entity identity are held only in volatile runtime maps and are absent from the persisted Manhunt round schema; startup recovery restores the round and players without rebuilding or sweeping those traps.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: An active persisted round is recoverable across runtime reload, but one of its player-created gameplay objects cannot be reconstructed from persisted state. Normal arena reset has explicit trap sweeping, while startup recovery does not perform equivalent reconciliation.
bugs.impact: Pre-reload traps cannot continue with authoritative gameplay state. If their entities survive the reload they can remain as orphan visuals with no proximity trigger; if they do not survive, the placed traps disappear. Either outcome changes the recovered round relative to its pre-reload state.
reproduction: Start an active Manhunt round as a Runner and place a Honey Trap.
Reload/restart the script or world while the active round is persisted.
Allow Manhunt startup recovery to restore the active round.
Inspect the previously placed trap and attempt to trigger it with a valid player path.
Confirm that the pre-reload trap gameplay state is not reconstructed from persisted Manhunt state.
bugs.expected: Active-round recovery should either restore each placed trap and its trigger state or deterministically remove/refund/reconcile pre-reload traps so world entities and gameplay state cannot diverge.
bugs.observed: Persisted schemaVersion 1 stores round/player/regen state but no placed trap list. Startup td() loads persisted state and restores player state via Wm(), but does not reconstruct traps or run the arena trap sweep used by normal reset.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Trap gameplay state lives in volatile arena trap/entity maps. Normal io()/Tp() cleanup can reconcile them during reset, but that path is absent from startup recovery.

relevantCode.reason: Trap state is runtime-only; ht()/Tu() omit traps; td() restores persisted rounds without trap reconstruction/sweep; io()/Tp() contain the normal cleanup path.

bugs.suggestedFix: Persist reconstructable trap state or explicitly sweep/reconcile all trap entities for recovered active arenas before gameplay resumes.

bugs.title: Runner loadout does not match the current Manhunt Guide
bugs.problem: The current Manhunt Guide describes Runner equipment including bow, arrows, swiftness, and trap, while the selected artifact gives Runner a knockback stick, cooked beef, Honey Traps, and temporary Speed; bow and arrows are assigned to Hunter.
bugs.whyThisIsBug: The Guide is the current map-specific gameplay authority supplied with v1.0.0. The implementation materially changes the asymmetric capabilities of both roles instead of merely renaming or visually changing equivalent items.
bugs.impact: Runner defensive/ranged options and Hunter offensive options differ from the documented game design. Players and testers following the Guide encounter different role balance, combat range, and survival strategy from what the current design document describes.
reproduction: Start Manhunt and inspect the Runner inventory/loadout after role assignment.
Record the Runner weapons, consumables, traps, and temporary effects.
Inspect the Hunter loadout in the same current artifact.
Compare both role loadouts with the current Manhunt Guide.
Confirm that bow/arrows are on Hunter while Runner receives knockback stick, beef, traps, and Speed instead of the Guide-described Runner bow/arrows/swiftness/trap set.
bugs.expected: Runner and Hunter capabilities should match the current approved Manhunt Guide, or the Guide should be explicitly updated if the implementation is the new approved design.
bugs.observed: Runner tu() grants knockback stick, 32 cooked beef, 3 traps, and placement Speed. Hunter nu() grants tracking compass, iron sword, bow, 64 arrows, and potions. The artifact contains only one minecraft:bow grant and it belongs to Hunter.
bugs.aiAnalysis: No alternate Runner bow/arrow grant exists in the selected artifact, so this is not a partial-loadout path missed by the audit.

relevantCode.reason: tu() defines Runner loadout; nu() defines Hunter loadout and contains the artifact's bow/arrow grant.

bugs.suggestedFix: Resolve the authority mismatch: either implement the Guide-approved Runner loadout or update/approve the Guide to match the intended v1.0.0 role design before treating the implementation as canonical.
